### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | This is Brill/De Gruyter Brill's PUBLISHER-WIDE policy (not Phronesis-specific — no journal-level AI statement found on the PHRO Instructions-for-Authors page, last revised 2025-11-10). Brill bans papers 'generated by AI/Machine Learning tools' (AI cannot be an author) and bans using generative AI to create or manipulate images/figures/research data. Simple proofreading/copy-editing with AI does not require disclosure. Any other significant AI contribution to the manuscript (e.g. assisting research design/methodology) must be disclosed in an acknowledgements section, documenting which tool and how it was used. Manuscript text must not be input into third-party AI/Grammarly-type tools due to confidentiality risk during review. Peer review itself must be done by humans only, not AI. Authors remain fully accountable for AI-assisted output (must fact-check it). |
| **Source URL** | https://www.degruyterbrill.com/publishing/for-authors/author-policies/artificial-intelligence ; https://brill.com/page/509467 |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes, with conditions (Brill is a RoMEO 'yellow' publisher for this journal). Author may self-archive the submitted (pre-peer-review) version at any time. Author may self-archive the accepted (post-peer-review, post-copyedit but not yet typeset) version with NO embargo period. Brill's own typeset/laid-out PDF must never be self-archived.
> Source: https://brill.com/fileasset/downloads_products/Author_Instructions/PHRO.pdf (Instructions for Authors, last revised 2025-11-10, section 'Author Fulfilment')

| Dimension | Assessment |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Textual/interpretive scholarship on ancient Greek and Roman philosophy from its origins through the end of the 6th century AD, covering metaphysics, epistemology, logic, psychology, and philosophy of science/medicine. Confirmed live examples (2023-2025): 'Wisdom, Political Expertise and the Unity of Virtues in Aristotle' (2024), 'Platonic Dualism Reconsidered' (2024), 'Technical Knowledge as Scientific Knowledge in Aristotle' (2025), 'Quantities or Qualities? A Forgotten Debate about Sounds between Ptolemy and Porphyry' (2023), plus Vol. 70(1) 2025 articles by Krizan, Chong and Weiss (titles not confirmed from search snippet, pp. 1-117) and a book note by Shaul Tor. No special-issue CFP found; the journal runs standard rolling submissions, not themed calls.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Close textual/philological analysis of primary Greek and Latin sources, History-of-philosophy interpretive argument (conceptual reconstruction, doxography), Philosophy of ancient science and medicine, Cross-school comparative work (e.g. Platonic vs. Aristotelian vs. Stoic doctrine), Book Notes (short review-essays; the journal does not run standard book reviews)

- **reviewer_culture (as a narrative, not the numeric data point given)**: No forum thread, Reddit post, or Chinese-language discussion (小木虫/知乎/fabiaoji) describing reviewer tone/culture was found; the field is filled only with the Endoxa numeric aggregate to avoid fabricating a narrative.
